Project Title: Advancing the Forecasting and Prediction of Atmospheric Rivers: Coupled Model Development, Physics Refinements, and Model Evaluations
Project Goal: The research activities will further accelerate NOAA capabilities to provide AR information with greater lead times, enhanced precision on intensity and landfalls, more accurate quantitative precipitation forecasts, and improved predictions of AR impacts for water resources management and disaster-risk reduction.
Research Keywords: Artificial Intelligence (AI) / Machine Learning (ML), Coupled Models & Techniques, Earth Prediction Innovation Center (EPIC), Reanalysis & Reforecasting, Parameterization, Precipitation Grand Challenge, Verification & Validation, Water in the West
Project Description: The proposed research activities for FY26 fall under three broad categories: i) research and development for physics-based model applications, ii) coupled AI model development and preparation of required training data, and iii) AI/ML and NWP model evaluation for atmospheric rivers.
Project Benefits: The two major deliverables are nested replay production for a period of 10-30 years depending on the computational resources and complete development of the coupled AI model for subseasonal scales, including the ensemble extension and higher resolution. Project will also start testing output of the AI models for downstream applications (e.g. snow pack, stream flow).

Project Title: Advancing the prediction of atmospheric rivers via enhanced physics parameterizations, data assimilation, and machine-learning models
Project Goal: The project has two main goals further develop a regional data-driven ensemble system for atmospheric river prediction and further develop a series of prototype MPAS-based atmospheric river forecast systems, dubbed MPAS-AR, with three supporting major objectives. 1) Develop more sophisticated physics parameterizations. 2) Advance ensemble prediction capabilities. and 3) Advance JEDI-based hourly cycled data assimilation (DA) capabilities.
Research Keywords: Artificial Intelligence (AI) / Machine Learning (ML), Atmospheric Physics, Model & Forecast Guidance, Water in the West
Associated Forecast Systems & Models: Model for Prediction Across Scales (MPAS), Unified Forecast System (UFS)
Project Description: The overall proposal goal is to improve the prediction of landfalling AR events in terms of precipitation type, timing, duration, and location. For MPAS-AR, we will develop improved physics parameterizations for the forecast challenges associated with atmospheric rivers (specifically warm-rain production and boundary-layer cloud representation), determine the optimal use of additional observation types in the DA system and evaluate their relative importance, and develop an initial ensemble prediction capability. For the regional data-driven modeling work, we will continue to explore the viability of AI-based models for increasing AR predictability, particularly probabilistically.
Project Benefits: Development and further enhancements to the MPAS-AR prototype forecast system, including its scale-aware physics, JEDI-based DA, and probabilistic components, will lead to improved AR forecast skill for both large- and small-scale features at longer lead times. In addition, the development of a high-resolution regional ensemble forecast capability within MPAS-AR will allow for an improved characterization of forecast uncertainty, which will be very beneficial to emergency managers and other officials tasked with making critical water-related decisions with differing lead-time constraints. Furthermore, the continued development of an AI-based model will augment traditional ensemble formulations, allowing potential further increases in both forecast skill and forecast uncertainty characterization. Datasets from these forecast components will also be beneficial to researchers examining methods for creating optimal decision support tools.

Project Title: Advancing Operational Water Prediction in the Western United States through Integrated AI Modeling and Hydrologic Testbeds, with Emphasis on Extreme Atmospheric Rivers and Improved Meteorological Forcings
Project Goal: The goal of this project is to advance NOAA's hydrologic forecasting capabilities for water predictions and decision making in the western United States through coordinated advances in data integration, modeling, evaluation, and testing in operational deployment environments.
Research Keywords: Artificial Intelligence (AI) / Machine Learning (ML), Reanalysis & Reforecasting, Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP), Satellite & Remote Sensing Technologies, Water in the West
Associated Forecast Systems & Models: Next Generation Water Resources Modeling Framework (NextGen)
Project Description: Advancing water prediction systems through integration and evaluation of emerging AI based data streams and modeling approaches.  Refine the CIROH model testbeds to support standardized evaluation and comparison of hydrologic model components, characterizing modeling limitations and accelerating CIROH research-to-operations advances.  Improve simulations of meteorological and hydrologic variables within the NextGen framework by developing AI-based downscaling methods. Develop a scalable, cloud-enabled hydrologic forecasting framework for CNRFC using NextGen philosophy to support operational, near real-time applications with emphasis on extreme atmospheric river events, including integration of high resolution meteorological forcings to improve hydrologic forecasts. Development and leveraging of observation-based and remote sensing derived snow products to improve hydrologic predictions in snow-dominated systems.
Project Benefits: The project delivers broad impacts to NOAA by strengthening the pathway from research innovation to sustained operational capability. Through close collaboration with industry partners, academic institutions, and NOAA operational staff, the research projects provide practical insight into how AI/MLenabled hydrologic models can be built, evaluated, and supported at operational scale. Tangible products including transition roadmaps, NextGencompatible specifications, and standardized evaluation frameworks directly address persistent barriers between research prototypes and operational adoption.
